speaker: Yama
devanagari:
हँसः शुचिषद्वसुरान्तरिक्षसद्-
होता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् ।
नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसद्
अब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत् ॥
iast:
ham̐saḥ śuciṣadvasurāntarikṣasad-
hotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat |
nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadvyomasad
abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ||
english: He is the swan in the bright sky, the bright one in the middle air, the priest at the altar, the guest in the house; he dwells in people, in the best, in truth, in the sky; born from water, from cattle, from truth, from mountains; he is truth, the great.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयत्यपानं प्रत्यगस्यति ।
मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते ॥
iast:
ūrdhvaṃ prāṇamunnayatyapānaṃ pratyagasyati |
madhye vāmanamāsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate ||
english: He leads the in-breath upward and drives the out-breath down. All the gods serve that dwarf seated in the middle.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः ।
देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥
iast:
asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ |
dehādvimucyamānasya kimatra pariśiṣyate |
etadvai tat ||
english: When this embodied one, dwelling in the body, slips away and is freed from the body, what remains here? This, truly, is that.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन ।
इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ ॥
iast:
na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana |
itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminnetāvupāśritau ||
english: No mortal lives by the in-breath or the out-breath. People live by something else, on which these two depend.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥
iast:
hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam |
yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama ||
english: Now, Gautama, I will tell you this secret, eternal Brahman, and what becomes of the self after reaching death.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः ।
स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् ॥
iast:
yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ |
sthāṇumanye'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam ||
english: Some embodied beings enter a womb to take on a body; others pass into a stationary thing, according to their deeds and according to their knowledge.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥
iast:
ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ |
tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate |
tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana |
etadvai tat ||
english: That person who is awake in those who sleep, shaping one desire after another: that is the bright, that is Brahman, that alone is called immortal. In it all the worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it. This, truly, is that.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥
iast:
agniryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo
rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva |
ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā
rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ||
english: As the one fire, entering the world, takes the form of each thing it meets, so the one Self within all beings takes the form of each, and is also outside.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥
iast:
vāyuryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo
rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva |
ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā
rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ||
english: As the one wind, entering the world, takes the form of each thing it meets, so the one Self within all beings takes the form of each, and is also outside.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः
न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः ।
एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥
iast:
sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣuḥ
na lipyate cākṣuṣairbāhyadoṣaiḥ |
ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā
na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ ||
english: As the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the faults that eyes see, so the one Self within all beings is not stained by the world's suffering, being outside it.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा
एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीराः
तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम् ॥
iast:
eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā
ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti |
tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāḥ
teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ||
english: The one controller, the Self within all beings, who makes his one form many: the wise who see him dwelling within themselves have lasting happiness, and no one else.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानाम्
एको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् ।
तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीराः
तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम् ॥
iast:
nityo'nityānāṃ cetanaścetanānām
eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān |
tamātmasthaṃ ye'nupaśyanti dhīrāḥ
teṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ||
english: The eternal among the impermanent, the consciousness of all that is conscious, the one who grants the desires of many: the wise who see him dwelling within themselves have lasting peace, and no one else.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् ।
कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा ॥
iast:
tadetaditi manyante'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham |
kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāṃ kimu bhāti vibhāti vā ||
english: 'This is that,' they feel: the highest joy, which cannot be described. How can I come to know it? Does it shine by itself, or shine in reflection?

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं
नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः ।
तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं
तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥
iast:
na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ
nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto'yamagniḥ |
tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ
tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ||
english: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars; these lightnings do not shine, let alone this fire. Everything shines after it as it shines; by its light all this is lit.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः ।
तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते ।
तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥
iast:
ūrdhvamūlo'vākśākha eṣo'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ |
tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate |
tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana |
etadvai tat ||
english: This is the ancient fig tree, with roots above and branches below. That is the bright, that is Brahman, that alone is called immortal. In it all the worlds rest, and no one goes beyond it. This, truly, is that.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यदिदं किं च जगत् सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् ।
महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥
iast:
yadidaṃ kiṃ ca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam |
mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyataṃ ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ||
english: All this world, whatever there is, has come forth from the breath of life and moves in it. It is a great terror, a raised thunderbolt. Those who know this become immortal.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः ।
भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः ॥
iast:
bhayādasyāgnistapati bhayāttapati sūryaḥ |
bhayādindraśca vāyuśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ ||
english: From fear of it fire burns; from fear the sun gives heat; from fear Indra and the Wind, and Death as the fifth, run their course.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्षरीरस्य विस्रसः ।
ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते ॥
iast:
iha cedaśakadboddhuṃ prākṣarīrasya visrasaḥ |
tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate ||
english: If one can come to know it here, before the body falls away, [one is freed]; otherwise one becomes fit to take a body again in the created worlds.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यथाऽऽदर्शे तथाऽऽत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके ।
यथाऽप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके
छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके ॥
iast:
yathā''darśe tathā''tmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke |
yathā'psu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke
chāyātapayoriva brahmaloke ||
english: As in a mirror, so in oneself; as in a dream, so in the world of the ancestors; as in water, so it appears in the world of the gandharvas; as shade and light, so in the world of Brahman.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् ।
पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥
iast:
indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvamudayāstamayau ca yat |
pṛthagutpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ||
english: Knowing that the senses are separate, arising separately, and that their rising and setting are their own, the wise do not grieve.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् ।
सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ॥
iast:
indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvamuttamam |
sattvādadhi mahānātmā mahato'vyaktamuttamam ||
english: Beyond the senses is the mind; beyond the mind is the intellect, the highest; beyond the intellect is the great self; beyond the great is the unmanifest, the highest.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च ।
यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति ॥
iast:
avyaktāttu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako'liṅga eva ca |
yaṃ jñātvā mucyate janturamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ||
english: Beyond the unmanifest is the Person, all-pervading and without any mark. Knowing him, a creature is freed and reaches immortality.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य
न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् ।
हृदा मनीषा मनसाऽभिक्लृप्तो
य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥
iast:
na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya
na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam |
hṛdā manīṣā manasā'bhiklṛpto
ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ||
english: His form is not within the range of sight; no one sees him with the eye. He is grasped by the heart, by insight, by the mind. Those who know this become immortal.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह ।
बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टते तामाहुः परमां गतिम् ॥
iast:
yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha |
buddhiśca na viceṣṭate tāmāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim ||
english: When the five senses come to rest together with the mind, and the intellect does not stir, that, they say, is the highest state.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् ।
अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥
iast:
tāṃ yogamiti manyante sthirāmindriyadhāraṇām |
apramattastadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau ||
english: This firm holding of the senses is what they call yoga. Then one must be vigilant, for yoga comes and goes.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा ।
अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते ॥
iast:
naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā |
astīti bruvato'nyatra kathaṃ tadupalabhyate ||
english: It cannot be reached by speech, nor by the mind, nor by the eye. How can it be grasped except by one who says, 'It is'?

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्यस्तत्त्वभावेन चोभयोः ।
अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धस्य तत्त्वभावः प्रसीदति ॥
iast:
astītyevopalabdhavyastattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ |
astītyevopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati ||
english: It should be grasped as 'It is', and also in its true nature. For one who has grasped it as 'It is', its true nature becomes clear.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते ॥
iast:
yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye'sya hṛdi śritāḥ |
atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute ||
english: When all the desires that dwell in one's heart are let go, then a mortal becomes immortal and reaches Brahman here.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
यथा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः ।
अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ॥
iast:
yathā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ |
atha martyo'mṛto bhavatyetāvaddhyanuśāsanam ||
english: When all the knots of the heart are cut here, then a mortal becomes immortal. This much is the teaching.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्य-
स्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका ।
तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति
विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति ॥
iast:
śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍya-
stāsāṃ mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtaikā |
tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti
viṣvaṅṅanyā utkramaṇe bhavanti ||
english: A hundred and one are the channels of the heart; one of them goes up to the crown of the head. Going up by it, one reaches immortality; the others lead in every direction at the time of departure.

speaker: Yama
devanagari:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा
सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः ।
तं स्वाच्छरीरात्प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण ।
तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति ॥
iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo'ntarātmā
sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ |
taṃ svāccharīrātpravṛhenmuñjādiveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa |
taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtamiti ||
english: The Person the size of a thumb, the inner Self, always dwells in the heart of people. One should draw him out from one's own body with steadiness, as the stalk is drawn from a reed. One should know him as the bright, the immortal; one should know him as the bright, the immortal.

speaker: Upanishad
devanagari:
मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा
विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् ।
ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्यु-
रन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव ॥
iast:
mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo'tha labdhvā
vidyāmetāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam |
brahmaprāpto virajo'bhūdvimṛtyu-
ranyo'pyevaṃ yo vidadhyātmameva ||
english: Having received this knowledge taught by Death, and the whole practice of yoga, Nachiketas reached Brahman, free of stain and free of death; and so will anyone else who knows the inner Self in this way.

speaker: teacher and student
devanagari:
सह नाववतु ।
सह नौ भुनक्तु ।
सह वीर्यं करवावहै ।
तेजस्विनावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॥
iast:
saha nāvavatu |
saha nau bhunaktu |
saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai |
tejasvināvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai ||
english: May he protect us both together. May he nourish us both together. May we work together with vigour. May our study be full of light. May we not hate each other.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
बोद्धारो मत्सरग्रस्ताः प्रभवः स्मयदूषिताः ।
अबोधोपहताश्चान्ये जीर्णमङ्गे सुभाषितम् ॥
iast:
boddhāro matsaragrastāḥ prabhavaḥ smayadūṣitāḥ |
abodhopahatāścānye jīrṇamaṅge subhāṣitam ||
english: Those who could understand are consumed by envy; the powerful are spoiled by pride; the rest are struck by ignorance. So fine sayings wither away within me.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
अज्ञः सुखमाराध्यः सुखतरमाराध्यते विशेषज्ञः ।
ज्ञानलवदुर्विदग्धं ब्रह्माऽपि तं नरं न रञ्जयति ॥
iast:
ajñaḥ sukhamārādhyaḥ sukhataramārādhyate viśeṣajñaḥ |
jñānalavadurvidagdhaṃ brahmā'pi taṃ naraṃ na rañjayati ||
english: An ignorant person is easily persuaded; an expert is persuaded more easily still; but someone puffed up by a scrap of knowledge, not even Brahma himself can win over.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
प्रसह्यमणिमुद्धरेन्मकरवक्त्रदंष्ट्रान्तरात्
समुद्रमपिसन्तरेत्प्रचलदूर्मिमालाकुलम् ।
भुजङ्गमपि कोपितं शिरसि पुष्पवद्धारयेत्
न तु प्रतिनिविष्टमूर्खजनचित्तमाराधयेत् ॥
iast:
prasahyamaṇimuddharenmakaravaktradaṃṣṭrāntarāt
samudramapisantaretpracaladūrmimālākulam |
bhujaṅgamapi kopitaṃ śirasi puṣpavaddhārayet
na tu pratiniviṣṭamūrkhajanacittamārādhayet ||
english: One might pull a jewel by force from between a crocodile's jaws, swim across an ocean tossed by rolling waves, or wear an angry snake on one's head like a flower; but one cannot win over the mind of an obstinate fool.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
लभेत सिकतासुतैलमपि यत्नतः पीडयन्
पिबेच्च मृगतृष्णिकासु सलिलं पिपासार्दितः ।
कदाचिदपि पर्यटन् शशविषाणमासादयेत्
न तु प्रतिनिविष्टमूर्खजनचित्तमाराधयेत् ॥
iast:
labheta sikatāsutailamapi yatnataḥ pīḍayan
pibecca mṛgatṛṣṇikāsu salilaṃ pipāsārditaḥ |
kadācidapi paryaṭan śaśaviṣāṇamāsādayet
na tu pratiniviṣṭamūrkhajanacittamārādhayet ||
english: Squeezing hard, one might get oil from sand; a thirsty person might drink water from a mirage; wandering about, one might even find a hare's horn; but one cannot win over the mind of an obstinate fool.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
व्यालं बालमृणालतन्तुभिरसौ रोद्धुं समुज्जृम्भते
छेत्तुं वज्रमणिञ्छिरीषकुसुमप्रान्तेन संनह्यते ।
माधुर्यं मधुबिन्दुना रचयितुं क्षाराम्बुधेरीहते
मूर्खान् यः प्रतिनेतुमिच्छति बलात् सूक्तैः सुधास्यन्दिभिः ॥
iast:
vyālaṃ bālamṛṇālatantubhirasau roddhuṃ samujjṛmbhate
chettuṃ vajramaṇiñchirīṣakusumaprāntena saṃnahyate |
mādhuryaṃ madhubindunā racayituṃ kṣārāmbudherīhate
mūrkhān yaḥ pratinetumicchati balāt sūktaiḥ sudhāsyandibhiḥ ||
english: Whoever tries to lead fools by force with nectar-sweet sayings is trying to bind a wild elephant with tender lotus fibres, to cut a diamond with the tip of a shirisha flower, or to sweeten the salt ocean with a drop of honey.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
स्वायत्तमेकान्तगुणं विधात्रा विनिर्मितं छादनमज्ञतायाः ।
विशेषतः सर्वविदां समाजे विभूषणं मौनमपण्डितानाम् ॥
iast:
svāyattamekāntaguṇaṃ vidhātrā vinirmitaṃ chādanamajñatāyāḥ |
viśeṣataḥ sarvavidāṃ samāje vibhūṣaṇaṃ maunamapaṇḍitānām ||
english: The Creator made a covering for ignorance that is always at one's command and wholly good: silence, the ornament of the unlearned, especially in a gathering of those who know.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं द्विप इव मदान्धः समभवं तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः।
यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतं तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥
iast:
yadā kiñcijjño'haṃ dvipa iva madāndhaḥ samabhavaṃ tadā sarvajño'smītyabhavadavaliptaṃ mama manaḥ|
yadā kiñcitkiñcidbudhajanasakāśādavagataṃ tadā mūrkho'smīti jvara iva mado me vyapagataḥ ||
english: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled with the thought 'I know everything'. When, little by little, I learned from the wise, the thought 'I am a fool' came, and my pride left me like a fever.
